sanskrit: athāpaśyan mahābāhur gandhamādanasānuṣu suramyaṃ kadalīṣaṇḍaṃ bahuyojanavistṛtam
english: Then that mighty-armed one beheld on the slopes of Gandhamādana a most beautiful grove of plantain trees stretching for many leagues.

sanskrit: tam abhyagacchad vegena kṣobhayiṣyan mahābalaḥ mahāgaja ivāsrāvī prabhañjan vividhān drumān
english: The immensely powerful Bhīma rushed toward it swiftly to disturb it, like a great rutting elephant breaking down trees of every kind.

sanskrit: utpāṭya kadalīskandhān bahutālasamucchrayān cikṣepa tarasā bhīmaḥ samantād balināṃ varaḥ
english: Tearing up plantain trunks as tall as many palm trees, Bhīma, foremost among the mighty, hurled them in all directions with great force.

sanskrit: tataḥ sattvāny upākrāman bahūni ca mahānti ca ruruvāraṇasaṃghāś ca mahiṣāś ca jalāśrayāḥ
english: Then many great creatures rushed at him — herds of deer and elephants, and water-buffalo that dwell near ponds.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghrāś ca saṃkruddhā bhīmasenam abhidravan vyāditāsyā mahāraudrā vinadanto 'tibhīṣaṇāḥ
english: Enraged lions and tigers also charged at Bhīmasena, their jaws gaping wide, terribly fierce, roaring most fearfully.

sanskrit: tato vāyusutaḥ krodhāt svabāhubalam āśritaḥ gajenāghnan gajaṃ bhīmaḥ siṃhaṃ siṃhena cābhibhūḥ talaprahārair anyāṃś ca vyahanat pāṇḍavo balī
english: Then the son of the Wind-god, Bhīma, relying on the strength of his own arms and filled with fury, crushed elephant with elephant and overwhelmed lion with lion; the mighty Pāṇḍava struck down the others with blows of his open palms.

sanskrit: te hanyamānā bhīmena siṃhavyāghratarakṣavaḥ bhayād visasṛpuḥ sarve śakṛnmūtraṃ ca susruvuḥ
english: Slaughtered by Bhīma, the lions, tigers, and hyenas all fled in terror, voiding dung and urine as they ran.

sanskrit: praviveśa tataḥ kṣipraṃ tān apāsya mahābalaḥ vanaṃ pāṇḍusutaḥ śrīmāñ śabdenāpūrayan diśaḥ
english: Having brushed them aside, the glorious and immensely powerful son of Pāṇḍu quickly entered the forest, filling all the directions with his roar.

sanskrit: tena śabdena cogreṇa bhīmasenaraveṇa ca vanāntaragatāḥ sarve vitresur mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
english: At that terrific sound, the roar of Bhīmasena, all the deer and birds within the depths of the forest trembled with fear.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdaṃ sahasā śrutvā mṛgapakṣisamīritam jalārdrapakṣā vihagāḥ samutpetuḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Suddenly hearing that sound stirring the beasts and birds, water-birds with damp wings rose up in their thousands.

sanskrit: tān audakān pakṣigaṇān nirīkṣya bharatarṣabhaḥ tān evānusaran ramyaṃ dadarśa sumahat saraḥ
english: Watching those flocks of water-birds, that bull of the Bhārata race followed them and beheld a most lovely and very great lake.

sanskrit: kāñcanaiḥ kadalīṣaṇḍair mandamārutakampitaiḥ vījyamānam ivākṣobhyaṃ tīrāntaravisarpibhiḥ
english: Golden groves of plantains trembling in the gentle breeze seemed to be fanning the unruffled lake as they spread along its banks.

sanskrit: tat saro 'thāvatīryāśu prabhūtakamalotpalam mahāgaja ivoddāmaś cikrīḍa balavad balī vikrīḍya tasmin suciram uttatārāmitadyutiḥ
english: Descending swiftly into that lake covered with abundant lotuses and lilies, the powerful Bhīma, of boundless splendour, sported in it like an unrestrained great elephant; and having played there for a long time he climbed out.

sanskrit: tato 'vagāhya vegena tad vanaṃ bahupādapam dadhmau ca śaṅkhaṃ svanavat sarvaprāṇena pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then, plunging swiftly into that forest full of trees, the Pāṇḍava blew his resonant conch with all his breath.

sanskrit: tasya śaṅkhasya śabdena bhīmasenaraveṇa ca bāhuśabdena cogreṇa nardantīva girer guhāḥ
english: At the blast of his conch, the roar of Bhīmasena, and the fierce clap of his arms, the caves of the mountain seemed to bellow in response.

sanskrit: taṃ vajraniṣpeṣasamam āsphoṭitaravaṃ bhṛśam śrutvā śailaguhāsuptaiḥ siṃhair mukto mahāsvanaḥ
english: Hearing that tremendous sound, like the crash of a thunderbolt, the great roar released by lions sleeping in the mountain caves arose.

sanskrit: siṃhanādabhayatrastaiḥ kuñjarair api bhārata mukto virāvaḥ sumahān parvato yena pūritaḥ
english: O Bhārata, the very great cry released by elephants terrified by the lion's roar filled the entire mountain.

sanskrit: taṃ tu nādaṃ tataḥ śrutvā supto vānarapuṃgavaḥ prājṛmbhata mahākāyo hanūmān nāma vānaraḥ
english: Hearing that sound, a foremost monkey who had been sleeping — a great-bodied monkey by the name of Hanūmān — stretched and yawned awake.

sanskrit: kadalīṣaṇḍamadhyastho nidrāvaśagatas tadā jṛmbhamāṇaḥ suvipulaṃ śakradhvajam ivocchritam āsphoṭayata lāṅgūlam indrāśanisamasvanam
english: Lying in the midst of the plantain grove, overcome by sleep, he yawned and lashed his enormous tail — raised aloft like Indra's banner — making a sound like Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tasya lāṅgūlaninadaṃ parvataḥ sa guhāmukhaiḥ udgāram iva gaur nardam utsasarja samantataḥ
english: The mountain re-echoed the thunderclap of his tail from all its cave-mouths on every side, like a cow bellowing its lowing.

sanskrit: sa lāṅgūlaravas tasya mattavāraṇanisvanam antardhāya vicitreṣu cacāra girisānuṣu
english: That sound of his tail, like the trumpeting of a maddened elephant, subsided and wandered across the varied ridges of the mountain.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenas taṃ śrutvā saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ śabdaprabhavam anvicchaṃś cacāra kadalīvanam
english: Bhīmasena, hearing that sound, his body hair bristling with excitement, ranged through the plantain forest seeking the source of the sound.

sanskrit: kadalīvanamadhyastham atha pīne śilātale sa dadarśa mahābāhur vānarādhipatiṃ sthitam
english: In the middle of the plantain grove, on a broad flat rock, that mighty-armed one beheld the lord of monkeys reclining.

sanskrit: vidyutsaṃghātaduṣprekṣyaṃ vidyutsaṃghātapiṅgalam vidyutsaṃghātasadṛśaṃ vidyutsaṃghātacañcalam
english: He was as hard to look upon as a mass of lightning, tawny as a mass of lightning, like a mass of lightning in his form, and restless as a mass of lightning.

sanskrit: bāhusvastikavinyastapīnahrasvaśirodharam skandhabhūyiṣṭhakāyatvāt tanumadhyakaṭītaṭam
english: His thick short neck was nestled between his arms crossed in a svastika; because his body was mostly shoulders, his waist and hips seemed slender.

sanskrit: kiṃ cic cābhugnaśīrṣeṇa dīrgharomāñcitena ca lāṅgūlenordhvagatinā dhvajeneva virājitam
english: With his head somewhat bowed and his long hair bristling, and his tail held aloft like a banner, he shone magnificently.

sanskrit: raktoṣṭhaṃ tāmrajihvāsyaṃ raktakarṇaṃ caladbhruvam vadanaṃ vṛttadaṃṣṭrāgraṃ raśmivantam ivoḍupam
english: His lips were red, his mouth with a copper-hued tongue, his ears red, his brows mobile; his face with its rounded fang-tips shone like the moon in full brilliance.

sanskrit: vadanābhyantaragataiḥ śuklabhāsair alaṃkṛtam kesarotkarasaṃmiśram aśokānām ivotkaram
english: Adorned within his face by gleaming white teeth mixed with tufts of hair, he resembled a cluster of aśoka blossoms.

sanskrit: hiraṇmayīnāṃ madhyasthaṃ kadalīnāṃ mahādyutim dīpyamānaṃ svavapuṣā arciṣmantam ivānalam
english: Resting amid golden plantain trees, blazing with great brilliance, glowing with his own body's light, he was like a flaming fire.

sanskrit: nirīkṣantam avitrastaṃ locanair madhupiṅgalaiḥ taṃ vānaravaraṃ vīram atikāyaṃ mahābalam
english: That foremost of monkeys, a hero of immense body and great strength, gazed without fear with his honey-tawny eyes.

sanskrit: athopasṛtya tarasā bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ siṃhanādaṃ samakarod bodhayiṣyan kapiṃ tadā
english: Then Bhīma of fearful valor swiftly approached and let out a lion's roar to rouse the monkey.

sanskrit: tena śabdena bhīmasya vitresur mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ hanūmāṃś ca mahāsattva īṣad unmīlya locane avaikṣad atha sāvajñaṃ locanair madhupiṅgalaiḥ
english: At Bhīma's sound the deer and birds trembled; Hanūmān, the great being, barely opening his eyes, then looked at him with a contemptuous gaze from his honey-tawny eyes.

sanskrit: smitenābhāṣya kaunteyaṃ vānaro naram abravīt kimarthaṃ sarujas te 'haṃ sukhasuptaḥ prabodhitaḥ
english: Addressing the son of Kuntī with a smile, the monkey said to the man: "For what reason have you roused me, who was sleeping peacefully, causing me pain?"

sanskrit: nanu nāma tvayā kāryā dayā bhūteṣu jānatā vayaṃ dharmaṃ na jānīmas tiryagyoniṃ samāśritāḥ
english: "Surely you who are learned should show compassion to all beings; we do not know dharma, we who are born in the animal womb.

sanskrit: manuṣyā buddhisaṃpannā dayāṃ kurvanti jantuṣu krūreṣu karmasu kathaṃ dehavākcittadūṣiṣu dharmaghātiṣu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ
english: "Human beings endowed with intelligence show compassion to living creatures — how then do the wise like yourself engage in cruel deeds, defiling body, speech, and mind, destroying dharma?"

sanskrit: na tvaṃ dharmaṃ vijānāsi vṛddhā nopāsitās tvayā alpabuddhitayā vanyān utsādayasi yan mṛgān
english: "You do not know dharma; the elders have not been attended by you; out of smallness of mind you destroy the wild creatures of the forest."

sanskrit: brūhi kas tvaṃ kimarthaṃ vā vanaṃ tvam idam āgataḥ varjitaṃ mānuṣair bhāvais tathaiva puruṣair api
english: "Tell me — who are you, and for what reason have you come to this forest shunned even by beings possessing human qualities, indeed shunned by all men?"

sanskrit: ataḥ paramagamyo 'yaṃ parvataḥ sudurāruhaḥ vinā siddhagatiṃ vīra gatir atra na vidyate
english: "Beyond this point this mountain is utterly impassable, O hero; without the movement of the perfected siddhas, there is no way forward here."

sanskrit: kāruṇyāt sauhṛdāc caiva vāraye tvāṃ mahābala nātaḥ paraṃ tvayā śakyaṃ gantum āśvasihi prabho
english: "Out of compassion and goodwill I warn you, O mighty one — you cannot go beyond this point; take comfort in that, O lord."

sanskrit: imāny amṛtakalpāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca bhakṣayitvā nivartasva grāhyaṃ yadi vaco mama
english: "Eat these roots and fruits fit for the immortals and turn back — if my words are worthy of acceptance."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vacas tasya vānarendrasya dhīmataḥ bhīmasenas tadā vīraḥ provācāmitrakarśanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of that wise lord of monkeys, the heroic Bhīmasena, crusher of enemies, then replied.

sanskrit: ko bhavān kiṃnimittaṃ vā vānaraṃ vapur āśritaḥ brāhmaṇānantaro varṇaḥ kṣatriyas tvānupṛcchati
english: "Who are you, and for what reason have you taken the form of a monkey? A Kṣatriya, second only to a Brāhmaṇa in rank, asks you this."

sanskrit: kauravaḥ somavaṃśīyaḥ kuntyā garbheṇa dhāritaḥ pāṇḍavo vāyutanayo bhīmasena iti śrutaḥ
english: "A Kaurava, born of the lunar dynasty, carried in the womb of Kuntī, a son of Pāṇḍu, son of the Wind-god, known as Bhīmasena — I am he."

sanskrit: sa vākyaṃ bhīmasenasya smitena pratigṛhya tat hanūmān vāyutanayo vāyuputram abhāṣata
english: Receiving Bhīmasena's words with a smile, Hanūmān, son of the Wind-god, spoke to that son of the Wind-god.

sanskrit: vānaro 'haṃ na te mārgaṃ pradāsyāmi yathepsitam sādhu gaccha nivartasva mā tvaṃ prāpsyasi vaiśasam
english: "I am a monkey; I will not give you the way you desire. Go well, turn back — lest you suffer harm."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca vaiśasaṃ vāstu yad vānyan na tvā pṛcchāmi vānara prayacchottiṣṭha mārgaṃ me mā tvaṃ prāpsyasi vaiśasam
english: Bhīma said: "Whatever harm may come — that is my affair; I do not ask you about it, O monkey. Give way, stand aside from my path, lest you suffer harm."

sanskrit: hanūmān uvāca nāsti śaktir mamotthātuṃ vyādhinā kleśito hy aham yady avaśyaṃ prayātavyaṃ laṅghayitvā prayāhi mām
english: Hanūmān said: "I have no strength to rise, for I am afflicted by illness. If you must go forward, then step over me and proceed."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca nirguṇaḥ paramātmeti dehaṃ te vyāpya tiṣṭhati tam ahaṃ jñānavijñeyaṃ nāvamanye na laṅghaye
english: Bhīma said: "The Paramātman, though without attributes, pervades and dwells within your body; I do not disrespect that which is to be known by knowledge and direct experience — therefore I will not step over you."

sanskrit: yady āgamair na vindeyaṃ tam ahaṃ bhūtabhāvanam krameyaṃ tvāṃ giriṃ cemaṃ hanūmān iva sāgaram
english: "Were I not to perceive through scripture the One who is the source of all beings, I would stride over you and this mountain, just as Hanūmān strode over the ocean."

sanskrit: hanūmān uvāca ka eṣa hanumān nāma sāgaro yena laṅghitaḥ pṛcchāmi tvā kuruśreṣṭha kathyatāṃ yadi śakyate
english: Hanūmān said: "Who is this Hanūmān by whom the ocean was stridden over? I ask you, O best of the Kurus — tell me if you are able."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca bhrātā mama guṇaślāghyo buddhisattvabalānvitaḥ rāmāyaṇe 'tivikhyātaḥ śūro vānarapuṃgavaḥ
english: Bhīma said: "A brother of mine, praised for his virtues, endowed with wisdom, sattva, and strength, greatly celebrated in the Rāmāyaṇa — a hero, foremost among monkeys."

sanskrit: rāmapatnīkṛte yena śatayojanam āyataḥ sāgaraḥ plavagendreṇa krameṇaikena laṅghitaḥ
english: "For the sake of Rāma's wife, the ocean stretching a hundred yojanas was crossed in a single leap by that lord of leaping monkeys."

sanskrit: sa me bhrātā mahāvīryas tulyo 'haṃ tasya tejasā bale parākrame yuddhe śakto 'haṃ tava nigrahe
english: "He is my brother of great heroism; I am his equal in energy, and in strength and valor in battle I am capable of restraining you."

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha dehi me mārgaṃ paśya vā me 'dya pauruṣam macchāsanam akurvāṇaṃ mā tvā neṣye yamakṣayam
english: "Rise and give me the way, or witness my manly prowess today — if you do not obey my command I shall send you to the realm of Yama."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vijñāya taṃ balonmattaṃ bāhuvīryeṇa garvitam hṛdayenāvahasyainaṃ hanūmān vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Recognizing him as intoxicated with strength and proud of his arm's prowess, Hanūmān laughed inwardly and spoke these words.

sanskrit: prasīda nāsti me śaktir utthātuṃ jarayānagha mamānukampayā tv etat puccham utsārya gamyatām
english: "Be appeased — I have no strength to rise, being oppressed by old age, O sinless one. Out of compassion for me, simply move this tail aside and proceed."

sanskrit: sāvajñam atha vāmena smayañ jagrāha pāṇinā na cāśakac cālayituṃ bhīmaḥ pucchaṃ mahākapeḥ
english: Then with a contemptuous smile, Bhīma grasped the tail with his left hand — yet he could not move the tail of the great monkey.

sanskrit: uccikṣepa punar dorbhyām indrāyudham ivocchritam noddhartum aśakad bhīmo dorbhyām api mahābalaḥ
english: He tried again to lift it with both arms — raised like Indra's weapon — yet even the immensely powerful Bhīma could not raise it with both arms.

sanskrit: utkṣiptabhrūr vivṛttākṣaḥ saṃhatabhrukuṭīmukhaḥ svinnagātro 'bhavad bhīmo na coddhartuṃ śaśāka ha
english: With eyebrows raised, eyes rolling, face contracted into a frown, and body drenched in sweat, Bhīma struggled — yet he utterly could not lift it.

sanskrit: yatnavān api tu śrīmāṃl lāṅgūloddharaṇoddhutaḥ kapeḥ pārśvagato bhīmas tasthau vrīḍād adhomukhaḥ
english: Though he strained with effort, exhausted by his attempt to lift the tail, the glorious Bhīma stood beside the monkey with his head bowed in shame.

sanskrit: praṇipatya ca kaunteyaḥ prāñjalir vākyam abravīt prasīda kapiśārdūla duruktaṃ kṣamyatāṃ mama
english: Then the son of Kuntī bowed down with joined palms and spoke: "Be gracious, O tiger among monkeys — may my harsh words be forgiven."

sanskrit: siddho vā yadi vā devo gandharvo vātha guhyakaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ san kāmayā brūhi kas tvaṃ vānararūpadhṛk
english: "Whether you are a siddha, a god, a gandharva, or a yakṣa — being asked, please tell me willingly who you are who bears the form of a monkey."

sanskrit: hanūmān uvāca yat te mama parijñāne kautūhalam ariṃdama tat sarvam akhilena tvaṃ śṛṇu pāṇḍavanandana
english: Hanūmān said: "O subduer of enemies, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas — since you have curiosity to know me fully, hear it all completely."

sanskrit: ahaṃ kesariṇaḥ kṣetre vāyunā jagadāyuṣā jātaḥ kamalapatrākṣa hanūmān nāma vānaraḥ
english: "I am the monkey named Hanūmān, born in the field of Kesarī by Vāyu, the life-breath of the world, O lotus-eyed one."

sanskrit: sūryaputraṃ ca sugrīvaṃ śakraputraṃ ca vālinam sarvavānararājānau sarvavānarayūthapāḥ
english: "Sugrīva son of the Sun and Vālin son of Indra — both kings of all monkeys, leaders of all monkey troops —

sanskrit: upatasthur mahāvīryā mama cāmitrakarśana sugrīveṇābhavat prītir anilasyāgninā yathā
english: "— those greatly heroic ones attended me as well, O crusher of enemies. My friendship with Sugrīva was like that of wind and fire."

sanskrit: nikṛtaḥ sa tato bhrātrā kasmiṃś cit kāraṇāntare ṛśyamūke mayā sārdhaṃ sugrīvo nyavasac ciram
english: "Then, wronged by his brother for some other reason, Sugrīva lived for a long time on Ṛśyamūka together with me."

sanskrit: atha dāśarathir vīro rāmo nāma mahābalaḥ viṣṇur mānuṣarūpeṇa cacāra vasudhām imām
english: "Then the heroic and immensely powerful Rāma, son of Daśaratha — Viṣṇu in human form — wandered upon this earth."

sanskrit: sa pituḥ priyam anvicchan sahabhāryaḥ sahānujaḥ sadhanur dhanvināṃ śreṣṭho daṇḍakāraṇyam āśritaḥ
english: "Seeking to fulfill his father's wish, accompanied by his wife and younger brother, bow in hand, foremost among archers, he took refuge in the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: tasya bhāryā janasthānād rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt vañcayitvā mahābuddhiṃ mṛgarūpeṇa rāghavam
english: "His wife was forcibly carried off from Janasthāna by Rāvaṇa, who had deceived the great-minded Rāghava by taking the form of a deer."

sanskrit: hṛtadāraḥ saha bhrātrā patnīṃ mārgan sa rāghavaḥ dṛṣṭavāñ śailaśikhare sugrīvaṃ vānararṣabham
english: "With his wife abducted, that Rāghava, searching for his wife together with his brother, saw Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, on a mountain peak."

sanskrit: tena tasyābhavat sakhyaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ sa hatvā vālinaṃ rājye sugrīvaṃ pratyapādayat sa harīn preṣayām āsa sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇe
english: "Friendship was formed between that great-souled Rāghava and Sugrīva; having killed Vālin he restored Sugrīva to the kingdom, and sent out the monkey hosts in search of Sītā."

sanskrit: tato vānarakoṭībhir yāṃ vayaṃ prasthitā diśam tatra pravṛttiḥ sītāyā gṛdhreṇa pratipāditā
english: "Then, from among the directions in which we set out with tens of millions of monkeys, news of Sītā was made known by a vulture in our direction."

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ śatayojanavistīrṇam arṇavaṃ sahasāplutaḥ
english: "Then I, for the accomplishment of the mission of Rāma whose deeds are effortless, leaped at once across the ocean stretching a hundred yojanas."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā sā ca mayā devī rāvaṇasya niveśane pratyāgataś cāpi punar nāma tatra prakāśya vai
english: "That goddess was seen by me in Rāvaṇa's abode, and I returned again, having made my name known there."

sanskrit: tato rāmeṇa vīreṇa hatvā tān sarvarākṣasān punaḥ pratyāhṛtā bhāryā naṣṭā vedaśrutir yathā
english: "Then the heroic Rāma, having slain all those rākṣasas, recovered his wife who had been lost, as the Vedic tradition recovers what has been forgotten."

sanskrit: tataḥ pratiṣṭhite rāme vīro 'yaṃ yācito mayā yāvad rāmakathā vīra bhavel lokeṣu śatruhan tāvaj jīveyam ity evaṃ tathāstv iti ca so 'bravīt
english: "Then, when Rāma was established in his kingdom, this hero was implored by me: 'O hero, O slayer of foes, as long as the tale of Rāma resounds in the worlds, may I live' — and he replied, 'So be it.'"

sanskrit: daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśa varṣaśatāni ca rājyaṃ kāritavān rāmas tatas tu tridivaṃ gataḥ
english: "Rāma caused his kingdom to be administered for ten thousand years and ten hundred years more, and then departed to heaven."

sanskrit: tad ihāpsarasas tāta gandharvāś ca sadānagha tasya vīrasya caritaṃ gāyantyo ramayanti mām
english: "Here the apsarases, dear one, and the gandharvas, O ever-sinless one, constantly delight me by singing the deeds of that hero."

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca mārgo martyānām agamyaḥ kurunandana tato 'haṃ ruddhavān mārgaṃ tavemaṃ devasevitam dharṣayed vā śaped vāpi mā kaś cid iti bhārata
english: "This path is impassable for mortals, O joy of the Kurus; therefore I have blocked your way along this road frequented by the gods, so that none may violate or curse it, O Bhārata."
